title: A switch in the parts list the walk cannot reach
goal: One of the scripted walks that checks the right hand panel stops partway through: it tries to press a switch in the Appearance list and the switch has scrolled out of reach, so the rest of that walk never runs and nothing after step 54 is being checked any more.
notes:
Pre-existing, NOT caused by the Appearance section gate change on 2026-09-08. Reproduced both ways.

WITH that change: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/parts-settings-inline-walk.json --no-build -> exit 1, [54 press] FAILED: the control "Switch" is not where a person could click it: it is off the window, or the dock has scrolled it far enough that the panel's edge cuts across the point a press would land on. Scroll to it with a "scrollPanel" step first.

WITHOUT it (git stash push -- Sources/Photonz/LayersPanel.swift, full rebuild): identical failure at step 54, same message. So the gate change is not the cause.

Likely the same class as the alignment-button task that landed on 2026-09-08 (44d95ca0 "Scroll to the alignment buttons instead of guessing a distance"): the walk needs a scrollPanel step rather than a guessed distance.
acceptance: The walk reaches the switch the way a person would rather than by assuming where the panel sits

log.note: Reproduced: step 54 press Switch in Border failed. Found the cause with a diagnostic walk that dumps the panel after every stage-5 press. Nothing scrolls in the outer dock; the Effects list scrolls INSIDE ITSELF. Re-opening the Shadow at stage 5 makes the list keep room for the effect just opened (877580bf/877580 the 2026-09-08 change), which slides the Border row up from y=469 to y=548, above the Effects header at y=503, so its switch is clipped by the section's own scroll area. inWindow goes false and the press is rightly refused.

Adversarial review before changing anything: is the walk being told the dock got worse? No. The stage-5 describe only claims the list reads as it did at stage 2, never that it is all on screen without scrolling, and scrolling back to a row that the list scrolled away from is exactly what a person does. Keeping the opened effect in view is deliberate and worth keeping. So reveal is the right answer here, not a source change.

Fixed: reveal in front of the Border switch press and the Shadow switch press in stage 5, and a reveal back to the Border row before the final picture so stage 5 frames what stage 2 framed. Seed and the stage-5 describe now say why the stage scrolls. Walk JSON only, no source changed.

Verified: walk finishes status ok in 68 steps (was failed at 53). The reveal reports 'brought into reach by scrolling 73pt' rather than a guessed number. panel-three-on.json and panel-back-as-drawn.json now match control for control, all 41, same names, details, positions and inWindow, so the walk's own claim that stage 5 reads exactly as stage 2 is machine-checked. parts (3/3) and effect (12/13) walks re-run; Scripts/test.sh green, 5278 tests.

Two follow-ups filed, both reproduced with commands and output in their notes: a-control-scrolled-out-of-its-own-section-gets-c (a walk can assert a control exists in a row it merely drifted under, and pass) and folding-an-effect-shut-in-a-short-window-does-no (effects-open-into-view-walk fails at step 12 on a clean tree, unrelated to this change).
